**Work context**

Shourya is a B.Tech Computer Science (AI/ML specialization) student at Galgotias College of Engineering and Technology, currently in their third year. Shourya is a member of the college coding club "Loop" and has completed a virtual AI internship from IBM.

**Personal context**

Shourya has a strong philosophy of learning by writing every line of code independently with full understanding — explicitly avoiding copy-pasting. Shourya has described feeling motivated to build something genuinely impressive and has a high-ambition, quality-over-speed approach to projects ("not jaw dropping, jaw breaking").

**Top of mind**

AuraOS v1 is now complete, with all core modules finished: activity tracking, SQLite memory, pattern analysis, personalized greetings, Windows notifications, FastAPI backend, and React/Vite frontend dashboard. Shourya's next horizon is evolving AuraOS into "FRIDAY" — a full AI companion with Gemini API integration, LangChain-powered autonomous agents, voice I/O, web research capability, and a cinematic UI — with quality prioritized over speed. A planned v2.0 envisions a Java (Spring Boot) middleware layer for high-performance concurrency and WebSocket real-time data, with Python retained for system data collection and AI inference.

**Brief history**

*Recent months*

Shourya applied for an AI/ML Engineer Intern role at Jio Institute, with AuraOS as the flagship project. During CV preparation, Shourya flagged and corrected an initial over-listing of AI/ML libraries — the verified skill set includes Python, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, FastAPI, SQLite, REST APIs, psutil, WMI, pycaw, React, Vite, Git, and GitHub. A six-day action plan was established for the application. Shourya also explored LangChain integration with AuraOS, covering model abstraction, SQLite memory wiring to LangChain interfaces, converting AuraOS modules into agent tools, and RAG over activity history using Chroma or FAISS with Google Generative AI embeddings. A live world intelligence dashboard (interactive map with AI-summarized news, market/weather data, cinematic dark UI) was discussed as a future AuraOS feature.

Career strategy conversations established AI engineering as Shourya's target path. An 18-month roadmap was developed across five phases: Foundation → Core AI Engineering (LLMs, RAG, vector databases, fine-tuning, model serving) → Specialization (AI Agents and Voice/Multimodal as primary tracks) → Portfolio → Go To Market. Key resources recommended: Andrej Karpathy's Neural Networks Zero to Hero, Chip Huyen's AI Engineering, LangGraph docs, fast.ai's Practical Deep Learning for Coders, and RAGAS. Building in public via daily GitHub commits and weekly LinkedIn posts was emphasized as non-negotiable.

A parallel Java strategy was also developed: Shourya has foundational Java knowledge (variables, data types, multithreading, error handling, classes, objects, collections framework) but acknowledged gaps in deeper internals. A learning path was laid out starting with implementing a HashMap from scratch, a custom ThreadPool, and a raw TCP chat server, leading toward an ambitious distributed infrastructure project called NEXUS (Raft consensus key-value store, custom message broker, secrets manager, API gateway, AI ops layer). The agreed sequencing: finish AuraOS first, then DSA (NeetCode 150, mornings) and NEXUS mini-projects (afternoons) in parallel. GitHub: github.com/vermashourya/AuraOS.

*Earlier context*

Shourya explored a cybersecurity roadmap covering six phases from networking/OS/crypto foundations through offensive security, defensive security, certifications (Security+, OSCP, CISSP), and career tracks (red team, SOC, threat intelligence, security engineering), with hands-on platforms like HackTheBox and TryHackMe recommended.

*Long-term background*

Shourya sought a strong semester project idea aligned with academic PEC evaluation criteria (patent or Scopus-indexed paper outcome, societal impact, IKS theme alignment). Top recommendations included a Blockchain-Based Ayurvedic Herb Traceability system and an Authenticity Validator for Academic Credentials. Shourya demonstrated a preference for comprehensive, defensible project structures from early on — a pattern consistent across all subsequent work.
